Benchmark identification on field photos

Source: R/benchmark.R
benchmarkKey.Rd

Measures how often photos are identified correctly, by one of three routes:

Usage

benchmarkKey(
  x,
  photos,
  model = NULL,
  route = NULL,
  top = 3,
  test = NULL,
  split = NULL,
  seed = 1,
  dir = NULL,
  prompt = "a photo of %s.",
  lineage = NULL,
  confidence = 0.8,
  k = 40,
  tiles = 4,
  method = "rpart",
  embeddings = NULL,
  reps = 1
)

Arguments

x

A dimoose key, or (for route = "build") a visionModel().

photos

The photos: the manifest inatPhotos() returns, the path of a manifest.csv (give dir too), or a data frame with path and label and optionally id and observation. Labels may be the key's results or just their scientific names. Without an observation column every photo counts as its own observation.

model

A visionModel().

route

"names", "key" or "build". By default "build" when x is a vision model, "key" for a key with machine tests and "names" for any other key.

top

Report the accuracy within this many guesses ("names" only: a key gives one answer).

test

Share of each species' observations to test with. By default 0.3 for "build" and all of them for the other routes, which learn nothing from the photos.

split

Instead of test: "train" or "test" for each photo, e.g. from splitByObservation(), to compare routes on the same test photos.

seed

Seed for the split and for finding sniglets.

dir

The folder the manifest's file column is relative to.

prompt, lineage, confidence

As in identifyPhotos(). lineage is optional and is never looked up here.

k, tiles, method

For "build": number of sniglets (discoverSniglets()), tiling (embedImages()) and tree method (keyFromSniglets()).

embeddings

For "build": the result of embedImages() for photos, if you have it already (rows in the same order).

reps

Number of splits to run. One split of a small sample says little: six test photos per species move a species' accuracy by 17 points each. With reps above 1 the benchmark is repeated with seeds seed, seed + 1, ..., each with a new split (and, for "build", a new key; the photos are embedded once), and the spread is reported. Needs a test share below 1, and no split.

Value

An object of class dimooseBenchmark, a list with

  • route, n (test photos), nTrain, observations (test observations);

  • accuracy: share of test photos identified correctly (top-1);

  • interval: its 95% Wilson interval (lower, upper), which treats the test photos as independent draws: read it as the least uncertainty there is, not all of it;

  • topK: named vector of the accuracy within 1, ..., top guesses;

  • perSpecies: for each species its number of test photos, top1 and (for "names") the accuracy within top guesses. Every species of the photos (and of the key) has a row; one without test photos has n = 0 and NA accuracies;

  • confusion: table of actual (rows) against predicted (columns), with the same species in the same order on both sides, so that the row sums are the n of perSpecies and the diagonal holds the correct answers. Any other answer has a column after them: a leaf that names several species, and "<none>" when a key gave no answer;

  • results: one row per test photo with id, observation, actual, predicted, rank (where the true species came in the ranking) and correct;

  • split: "train" or "test" for every photo given;

  • with reps above 1, all of the above describe the first split, and there are also repeats (one row per split: rep, seed, n, nTrain, correct, accuracy), accuracyMean, accuracySd (the standard deviation between splits) and accuracyRange, and perSpecies gains top1Mean, the species' accuracy over all splits' test photos together. The splits share photos, so they are not independent samples: the spread shows how much one split can mislead, it is not a standard error;

  • key (for "build", the key that was built) and identify (for "names" with a lineage: the identifyPhotos() answers with correct, and the shares that were confident and correct).

Details

  • "names": the model ranks the key's own species for each photo from their names alone (suggestSpecies()); nothing is learned from the photos. With a lineage the answers of identifyPhotos(), which fall back to the genus, family or order when the species is uncertain, are scored too.

  • "key": a key with machine tests (from keyFromSniglets() or keyFromClusters()) is followed for each photo (scoreImages(), evaluateKey()).

  • "build": a photo key is built from the training photos (sniglets found in them, then keyFromSniglets()) and followed for the test photos. This is the route to use for "how good a key can be learned from photos like these".

Training and test photos are divided by observation with splitByObservation(), never photo by photo.

See also

inatPhotos(), evaluateKey(), looKey()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
key <- montanaKey()
photos <- inatPhotos(key, n = 20, dir = file.path(tempdir(), "inat"))
model <- visionModel(name = "bioclip-2")
benchmarkKey(key, photos, model)                    # species ranked from their names
benchmarkKey(model, photos)                         # a key built from 70% of the observations
} # }
